paper.title: Contextual Bandits with Latent Confounders: An NMF Approach

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with latent confounders (U = AW)
unmapped: L observed contexts drawn i.i.d. with probabilities beta_s; mean reward matrix U (L x K) factorizes as U = AW with non-negative A (L x m, row-stochastic, separable) and W (m x K): latent confounder of cardinality m
learner knows latent dimension m and min context probability beta, and WStRIP constants rho_1, rho_2
A satisfies l2-WStRIP and W satisfies l1-WStRIP
settings.definition_quote: At each time t the algorithm observes a context S_t = s_t; After observing the context the algorithm selects an arm A_t = a_t ... The algorithm then obtains a Bernoulli reward Y_t with mean U_{s_t,a_t}. ... Therefore, we have U = AW.

unmapped: L observed contexts, uniform context distribution; mean reward matrix U = AW with latent dimension m
settings.definition_quote: Consider a problem instance (U,A,W) such that beta_s = 1/L for all s and |C(z_i)| = L/m ...

symbols.m_lat: cardinality m of the latent confounder (rank of U)

conditions: A satisfies l2-WStRIP with constants (delta/L, rho_2, m_1')
W satisfies l1-WStRIP with constants (delta, rho_1, m_2')
Delta = min gap over contexts, constant

source.label: thm:existence
source.quote: Consider the bandit model with reward matrix U = AW. Suppose A is separable. Let A satisfy l2-WStRIP with constants (delta/L, rho_2, m_1') while W satisfies l1-WStRIP with constants (delta, rho_1, m_2'). Let m' = max(m'_1,m'_2) = Theta(m log(K)). Suppose beta_s = Omega(1/L) for all s. We also assume that L = Omega(K log(K)). Then there exists a randomized algorithm whose regret at time T is bounded as R(T) = O(L poly(m,log K)/Delta^2 log T) with probability at least 1-delta. Here poly(m,log K) = O(m^5 log^2 K).

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards (pseudo-regret) against per-context best arm; the 1-delta probability is over the algorithm's random choice of subsets. Restated with details as Theorem 8.

symbols.theta: exploration constant, theta >= 4 max(2m'((16+Delta)rho_2+32m)/(Delta rho_1 rho_2), 15/(rho_1(1-lambda)))^2
symbols.lambda_W: robustness parameter lambda in Hottopix condition

conditions: U = AW, contexts arrive independently with probability beta_s
W satisfies l1-WStRIP with parameters (delta, rho_1, 2m')
A in [0,1]^{L x m} satisfies l2-WStRIP with parameters (delta/L, rho_2, 2m') and is separable

source.label: thm:mainub
source.quote: ... then with probability atleast 1-delta, Algorithm 1 with epsilon_t = min(1, theta(2m'+m)/(beta t)) and gamma(t) = max(1/t, 2/sqrt(theta)) has regret, R(T) <= theta(m+2m')log(T)/beta + 4(L+K+1)m' log(T) + o(1) = O(L poly(m,m')/Delta^2 log T) = O(L m^5 log^2 K/Delta^2 log T)

results.notes: o(1) term dropped from the expression. The O form equals Theorem 1 (r1).

symbols.D_U: instance constant D(U) = O(1/Delta) depending on entries of U, independent of L,K,m
symbols.alpha_c: consistency exponent alpha in (0,1) of alpha-consistent policies

conditions: |C(z_i)| = L/m for all latent contexts, m divides L
C(z_i) disjoint for distinct latent contexts

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: Consider a problem instance (U,A,W) such that beta_s = 1/L for all s and |C(z_i)| = L/m (assume that m divides L) for all z_i. Further, we assume that C(z_i) cap C(z_j) = emptyset ... Then the regret of any alpha-consistent policy is lower-bounded as follows, R(T) >= (K-1)mD(U)((1-alpha)(log(T/2m) - log(L/m)) - log(4KC)) for any T > tau

results.notes: Same statement appears as Theorem 4 in the main text (existence of instance with beta_s = Omega(1/L)). Lower bound for a specific instance class; alpha-consistent policies (algorithm_class other).
